insight.title: Why Complicated Explanations Usually Hide a Lack of Knowledge
insight.subtitle: How to spot when someone is covering up what they do not know
insight.notificationHook: Complexity is often a shield for ignorance

sections.text: When ancient cartographers reached the edge of their known world, they didn’t leave blank spaces. Instead, they drew terrifying sea monsters. They used dramatic illustrations to disguise their lack of actual information.
We do the exact same thing today. When people don’t understand a project, market, or problem, they rarely admit it. Instead, they use dense jargon and over-complicated plans to shield themselves.

This means complexity is often a defensive reaction, not a sign of expertise. True mastery simplifies; insecurity overcomplicates to prevent you from asking questions that might expose their lack of depth.
Try this today: When you hear someone use heavy jargon today, look for the blank space they are hiding.
The next time someone confuses you, remember they might just be drawing dragons.
